title: Ryu Plugin Manifest
description: The manifest.json schema for Ryu apps. Defines runnables, permissions, activation events, and marketplace metadata.
$comment: HAND-MAINTAINED — this is the author-facing doc schema served at https://ryuhq.com/schemas/plugin.json, deliberately NOT the machine-generated contract. The generated one is crates/core/kernel-contracts/schemas/plugin-manifest.schema.json (blessed by `RYU_REGEN_SCHEMAS=1 cargo test -p ryu-kernel-contracts`, consumed by the TS SDK's `generate:contracts`); it carries every internal field plus rustdoc intra-doc links, so it is the wrong thing to hand a plugin author. This file must track these Rust types in crates/core/kernel-contracts/src/manifest.rs: PluginManifest, RunnableEntry, Surface, CompanionSurface, Contributes, TurnHookContribution, HookMatch, McpServerDecl, SettingsTabContribution, SettingsFieldContribution, SettingsFieldType, SettingsFieldOption, SettingsScope, ToolFilterContribution, Requires, CapabilityReq. Three deliberate divergences, all the same shape — Rust is permissive at the parse boundary so one bad string cannot take a whole manifest down, while this schema is strict so the author is told at authoring time instead of shipping something inert: (1) TurnHookContribution.on is a bare `String` in Rust and unknown phases are dropped at dispatch, but here it is enum-constrained to the 16 phases Core actually fires — hand-synced from the `pub const ON_*` declarations in apps/core/src/plugin_host/mod.rs; a permissive `type: "string"` here is exactly what let authors ship hooks Core silently never fires, so add a phase here only after the const exists there. (2) SettingsFieldType and (3) SettingsScope both fall back (to text / node) via custom deserializers in Rust, but each list is a transcription of a closed renderer switch, so an unrecognised value is an author typo worth flagging, not forward-compat. Deliberately NOT documented, because none are hand-written by a plugin author: `backend_code` / `backend_sha256` / `ui_code_sha256` are computed by `ryu pack` / `ryu publish`; `source` and `runtime` are set by the installer; `permissions`, `surfaces`, `icon`, `banner`, `accentColor`, `iconBackground` and `iconDither` exist on PluginManifest but are unused by all 80 first-party manifests, so documenting them here would be transcription without a single example to check against — take them from the generated schema if that changes. The root object is intentionally open (no additionalProperties:false): closing it would reject those legitimate unlisted fields and every future one. Verify this file by validating every built-in manifest against it — apps-store/*/manifest.json and plugins-store/*/manifest.json (where the packaged ones live; Core include_str!s them from there) plus the ~13 Core-only apps/core/src/plugin_manifest/fixtures/*.manifest.json — all 72 pass as of this revision, and a regression there is the cheapest signal that the Rust moved.

id.description: Unique app identifier, and also the directory name the app is installed under — which is why the alphabet is a strict allowlist rather than a blocklist: it is a path-traversal sink. Both bare-kebab (ghost, data-grid-explorer) and dotted reverse-domain (com.ryu.mail, com.example.research-assistant) forms are accepted. Allowed characters a-z A-Z 0-9 . - _; no '..' anywhere; no leading '.' or '-'; no trailing '.'; at most 128 bytes.

ui_code_sha256.description: Hex SHA-256 of bundled sandboxed UI code. Computed by ryu pack/ryu publish. Absent for manifest-only plugins.

permission_grants.description: Permission declarations this plugin needs (e.g. mcp:web_search). Enforcement is the Gateway's responsibility.

mcp_servers.description: Declarative stdio MCP servers this plugin registers into Core's MCP registry on enable (and deregisters on disable/uninstall). Keyed by the server name the registry uses — the same key a user's mcp.json would use, and a user mcp.json entry with that name still wins. This is how a plugin ships agent tooling instead of Core baking a built-in server in.

companion.description: Optional in-desktop overlay or sidebar panel surface.

activation_events.description: VS-Code-style activation events: *, onStartup, onChat, onCommand:<id>. Empty = eager.

contributes.description: Contribution points: turn hooks + declarative UI widgets.

requires.description: Plugin-to-plugin dependencies. Core resolves topological enable order.

targets.description: Host surfaces this plugin runs on. Empty = runs on every surface.

engines.description: The Core version this plugin needs — the plugin-to-Core edge, as opposed to the plugin-to-plugin edge in `requires`.

sidecars.description: Declarative managed sidecars the plugin ships (the app-to-sidecar bridge): long-running child processes Core downloads/provisions, spawns and health-monitors, exactly like a built-in sidecar. Gated at enable by the sidecar:process grant — automatic for Core-tier apps, an approved grant for community ones.

provides.description: Capabilities this plugin SERVES — the other half of requires.capabilities. Binds an abstract capability name to a concrete serving surface on this manifest, so the broker can route a consumer's call to it without the consumer knowing which app answers.

description.description: Longer description shown in the marketplace detail dialog.

tagline.description: Short one-line pitch shown under the name.

category.description: Taxonomy category beyond the runnable kinds.

iconUrl.description: Square logo/icon URL for the listing card.

capabilities.description: Human-readable capability strings. When omitted, derived from permission_grants.

examplePrompts.description: Example prompt chips shown on the marketplace detail page.

RunnableMeta.description: One Runnable entry inside the manifest (Rust: RunnableEntry).

id.description: Stable unique identifier within this app (e.g. tool-web-search).

kind.description: Discriminant that determines which per-kind config shape is required.

config.description: Per-kind configuration. Some kinds (agent) treat this as optional and apply defaults; others (tool, workflow) require it.

RunnableKind.description: The kind of Runnable — the union of every executable thing in Ryu. agent: system prompt + tools + model/engine binding. workflow: a DAG of typed nodes. tool: a callable tool. skill: an Agent Skill. companion: an in-desktop overlay or sidebar surface. channel: a channel bot adapter (Telegram, Slack, WhatsApp, Discord). engine: a pluggable model/inference engine binding. policy: a Gateway policy fragment (firewall rule, DLP filter, budget cap).

Surface.description: A host surface the plugin can run on.

CompanionSurface.description: Companion surface descriptor — an optional in-desktop overlay or sidebar panel an app registers. The fields mirror the UX primitives a companion widget needs; everything but label is optional.

label.description: Display label for the companion panel tab or tooltip.

icon.description: Icon identifier, resolved by the desktop shell.

Contributes.description: Contribution points for turn hooks and declarative UI.

turn_hooks.description: Server-side turn hooks: JS that Core runs in the plugin sandbox at a turn boundary and that returns a directive. Self-contained — a hook carries its own inline code and is NOT cross-referenced against runnables.

composer_controls.description: UI controls added to the chat composer.

settings_tabs.description: Settings tabs contributed to the desktop settings dialogs. A tab is EITHER declarative (fields bound to preference keys, drawn by the shared renderer) OR a named view the shell resolves to a bespoke component — a tab with neither is rejected at import.

tool_filters.description: Tools this plugin wants withheld from the model's offered tool list — the declarative half of a tool firewall. Not a security boundary: hiding a tool does not revoke the capability, it only stops the tool being advertised. Enforcement stays with permissions and grants.

slash_commands.description: Slash commands available in the chat input.

TurnHookContribution.description: One server-side chat turn hook. The body is a JS fragment run in the plugin sandbox with `ctx` (the turn context) and `host` (the capability bridge: host.sideModel, host.storage, host.log) in scope; it returns a directive such as {kind:"none"}, {kind:"note",text} or {kind:"continue",text}. Declare the body EITHER as `code_file` (recommended: a path to a real .js file you can read, lint and diff) OR inline as `code` — exactly one, never both.

id.description: Stable id for this hook (used in logging/audit), unique within the plugin.

on.description: The turn boundary this hook fires on. Only these phases exist — Core dispatches by exact string match, so a phase spelled any other way is a hook that never runs. `stop` is an accepted alias of `post_assistant_turn` (Claude's naming). post_tool_use, subagent_stop, session_end, notification, model_select and session_tree are observation-only: their directives are not applied.

code.description: The JS hook body inline. This is the WIRE form: `ryu pack` produces it by reading `code_file`, which is what keeps the whole body inside the Gateway-signed surface. Writing it by hand still works, but prefer `code_file` — a multi-kilobyte \n-escaped JSON string is not reviewable, and unreviewable code is where malicious behaviour hides.

code_file.description: Path to the file holding the hook body, relative to the plugin root, e.g. "hooks/review.js". Must be exactly `hooks/<name>.js` (or .mjs) — one directory deep, no traversal. The file is a FRAGMENT, not an ES module: Core splices it into an async IIFE, so a top-level `return` is correct and an `export` is not. Core resolves it at load time; `ryu pack` inlines it into `code` when bundling.

match.description: Optional cheap pre-gate, evaluated in Rust before the sandbox is spawned. Absent (or all fields empty) means the hook always runs.

HookMatch.description: A pre-gate for a turn hook. Conditions are OR-ed: the hook runs if any present condition matches. Exists purely to skip the sandbox spawn on turns where the hook provably cannot act — richer matching belongs inside the hook JS.

flag.description: Run only when the request set this composer flag true (ctx.flags[flag]), e.g. io.ryu.double-check.

commands.description: Run when the trimmed last user message starts with any of these prefixes, e.g. ["/goal"]. This is how a slash-command hook wakes up.

stateful.description: Run when the plugin has stored state for this conversation (a value keyed by conversation_id in its default KV namespace), e.g. an active goal.

tools.description: For pre_tool_use / post_tool_use / tool_result hooks: run when the tool being called matches any of these patterns. A pattern is a tool id with optional leading/trailing * ("*" = every tool, "bash*" = ids starting with bash).

McpServerDecl.description: One declarative stdio MCP server. Spawned per request as `command args…`.

command.description: Executable to spawn (e.g. npx, an absolute path, or a ~/.ryu/bin name).

command_env.description: Name of an env var whose value, when set, OVERRIDES command with an absolute binary path (e.g. RYU_GHOST_BIN). Lets a plugin ship a bare command that Core repoints at a profile-specific downloaded binary. Absent means use command verbatim.

env.description: Extra environment variables for the server process.

description.description: Human description shown by the MCP listing endpoint.

enabled.description: When false the server is registered but skipped by list/call. Defaults true so a bare { command } entry just works.

SettingsTabContribution.description: One settings tab. Declare either fields or view — a tab with neither is rejected at import rather than silently dropped by the renderer.

id.description: Stable id for this tab within the plugin; the settings nav routes to it. Required — the desktop's <plugin>.settings fallback collides the moment a plugin declares a second tab.

scope.description: Which settings dialog this tab lands in. Anything unrecognised falls back to node.

view.description: A rich settings view this app ships instead of declarative fields. The settings renderer owns the vocabulary and resolves the name to a component (first-party) or a sandboxed UI (third-party).

fields.description: The declarative fields this tab renders. Empty is only legal alongside a view.

SettingsScope.description: Where the tab's preferences live. A node preference is stored on the node and is therefore shared by EVERY user of that node; a user preference is client-local. Default node, which is the historical behaviour — a per-user knob has to say so.

SettingsFieldType.description: The control this field renders as. This list is the desktop renderer's control switch — an unrecognised type falls back to a plain text input. `model_picker` stores a bare model id; `agent_picker` stores the full selection the chat composer can express (agent, provider, model, thinking level, effort, access mode) as an AgentSelection JSON object. Either one, left unset, inherits the node-wide default selection. `secret` is the BYOK control and the one variant that does NOT persist to preferences: it is write-only and masked, submitted to PUT /api/plugins/{id}/secrets/{key} and stored encrypted at rest, never read back (the renderer can only ask whether a secret is Set). Because the stored value is what a manifest's `secret_headers` `env:VARNAME` token falls back to, its `pref_key` must be the ENV VAR NAME the manifest already names (e.g. RYU_TAVILY_API_KEY), not a dotted preference key.

SettingsFieldOption.description: One choice for a select field. A bare string means value and label are the same — the form every hand-written manifest reaches for.

value.description: The value persisted to the preference key.

label.description: Display label. Absent shows the raw value.

SettingsFieldContribution.description: One configurable field, bound to exactly one preference key. The default/required/min/max/min_length/max_length block is validation metadata cross-checked against type at import — declaring a min on a toggle is an error, because validation that is silently ignored reads as a guarantee that was never enforced.

type.description: The control to render. Absent means a plain text input.

pref_key.description: The preference key this field reads/writes via /api/preferences/:key. Also the field's identity, so two fields in one tab may not share it. Restricted to a path-safe alphabet — it becomes a URL path segment.

label.description: Display label. Absent shows the pref_key.

description.description: Helper caption shown under the field.

placeholder.description: Placeholder for text and model-picker inputs.

options.description: Choices for a select field; required for that type and inert for every other one.

default.description: Default value in the field's own JSON type (boolean for a toggle, number for a number, string elsewhere) — NOT the stringified form preferences are stored in, so the manifest stays readable and the type is checkable.

required.description: Whether the user must supply a value. Advisory: enforced by the renderer, declared here so the contract is one place.

min.description: Inclusive lower bound for a number field.

max.description: Inclusive upper bound for a number field.

min_length.description: Minimum length for a text/textarea value.

max_length.description: Maximum length for a text/textarea value.

ToolFilterContribution.description: One tool id withheld from the model's offered tool list.

tool.description: Fully-qualified tool id (<server>__<tool>, e.g. browser__navigate), optionally ending in * to hide every tool with that prefix (shadow__* hides a whole server). The namespace is mandatory — a bare navigate is ambiguous across servers and is rejected at import. A trailing * is the only wildcard position allowed: an interior or leading * invites a pattern that silently matches far more than the author pictured.

reason.description: Why the plugin hides it. Surfaced in the plugin's listing so a user can see what a plugin removes from the model's view before installing it.

Requires.description: Plugin-to-plugin dependencies. Distinct from engines, which constrains plugin-to-Core. Absent means no dependencies — the plugin enables standalone.

apps.description: Other plugins that must be installed, and are auto-enabled in dependency order, before this one can enable.

capabilities.description: Abstract capability requirements (e.g. rag, memory, tts) the capability broker resolves to a concrete provider app at bind time. Distinct from apps: an apps edge names a specific plugin id, a capabilities edge lets the binding registry — or the user — pick which enabled provider serves it.

grants.description: Permission grants required from the Gateway.

id.description: The id of the plugin this one depends on.

min_version.description: Optional MINIMUM version the dependency must satisfy. A bare version ("1.2.0") means ">=1.2.0" — deliberately not semver's default caret, which would reject 2.0.0. Explicit comparator syntax (">=1.2, <2", "^1.2", "~1.2") is honoured verbatim.

capability.description: The capability name (e.g. rag, tts), matched against a provider's declared capability.

min_version.description: Optional minimum CAPABILITY version the bound provider must satisfy (bare "1.2.0" = ">=1.2.0"). Checked against the provider's declared capability version, not against the provider plugin's own semver. Absent means any version is acceptable.

EnginesReq.description: The required Ryu version, mirroring VS Code's engines.vscode.

ryu.description: Semver requirement the running Core version must satisfy (e.g. ">=0.3.0", "^1.2"). An unparseable value, or one the running Core does not satisfy, makes the loader reject the manifest.

ProvidesEntry.description: One capability this plugin serves. The broker forwards a consumer's /api/host/capability/<capability> call to the named sidecar's route using the PROVIDER's minted token — the consumer never sees it.

capability.description: The capability name served (e.g. rag). Consumers match on this in their requires.capabilities.

version.description: The capability's own semver version, independent of the plugin version, so a consumer's min_version floor is checked against the capability contract rather than the app release.

sidecar.description: The local name of one of this manifest's sidecars that serves the capability; cross-validated at import. Absent means an in-process capability the broker declines to proxy.

route.description: The proxied sub-path on that sidecar's http spec the broker forwards capability calls to (e.g. /rag/query). Cross-validated against the sidecar's declared routes.

grant.description: The Gateway-approved grant a consumer must hold to invoke this capability. Absent means no grant beyond declaring the edge.

SidecarSpec.description: One managed sidecar process. The nested process/http/host_api payloads are intentionally left open here — they are large, evolve fastest, and the generated contract at crates/core/kernel-contracts/schemas/plugin-manifest.schema.json is their authority. This def pins the parts an author gets wrong most.

name.description: Local name, unique within the plugin. Namespaced to <plugin_id>/<name> by Core, and the key provides.sidecar references.

process.description: How Core obtains and runs the process. Tagged by kind so a future runtime is a data change, not a code change.

kind.description: binary: a checksum-verified download placed in the plugin's bin/ dir. python: the external-runtime provisioner (venv + pip + assets), then python -m <entry>. local: an already-present command on PATH or resolved from an env var. node: a bundled JS entrypoint.

port.description: TCP port the process's HTTP server binds to; used to build the health-check URL and the proxy target.

health_path.description: Health-check path on the process's server.

lazy.description: Spawn on first use instead of at plugin-enable.

idle_stop_secs.description: Scale-to-zero timeout in seconds: stop the sidecar after this long with no traffic. Absent means it stays up.

http.description: Optional HTTP proxy declaration. public_mount is the generic ext-proxy surface clients reach at /api/ext/<plugin_id>/… — the reason an app never needs a bespoke route baked into Core.

host_api.description: Optional host-API declaration: the subset of the owning plugin's approved grants this sidecar may call back into Core with.

provides_provider.description: Optional model-provider declaration, for a sidecar that serves an OpenAI-compatible inference endpoint Core should register as a provider.

field.description: The configuration field this step maps to.
